newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes rebound late with ACCESS, eye storms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes rebound late with ACCESS, eye storms.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes rebounded late Wednesday finding support from overnight ACCESS and some bullish sentiment concerning a new storm likely to threaten Gulf Coast and Caribbean oil installations.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $21.70-80 a barrel, about 30 cents higher than Tuesday.
Outright prices late Tuesday had been hit by large builds in U.S. crude stocks, around 10 million barrels.
But news that Iraq may be massing troops on its border with the Kurdish regions in the north of the country, helped the market regain its footing, boosting prices to $22.10/bbl.
Midland/WTI saw sales at 8 cts over WTI/Cushing, 1 cts higher than earlier deals.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was steady around 28 cts over the WTI/Cushing, with Heavy Lousiana Sweet/Empire quiet, talked at 17-20 cts over WTI.
Sour grades were slightly active, with West Texas Sour/Midland done at $1.27 under WTI/Cushing and Eugene Island at $1.15 below the same WTI/Cushing.
But traders said the appearance of Urals in the U.S. Gulf and other shipments from Latin America would hurt sours soon.
"By the end of Oct scheduling, I'm willing to bet we'll be down to minus $1.80, and it will stay there," a trader said.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus was done as high as $2.15, and was talked at $2.15-$2.18, after being done earlier at $2.09.
